transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… things at work have been feeling off. Dispatch and compliance seem to be watching my route changes through the computer system, and there are little comments over the radio that feel like they’re about me. People say it’s just normal oversight, but… I can tell some drivers are reporting on me.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
I don’t know… not really. I mean, I hear things over the radio or at work, but if you mean like a voice in an empty room, I’m not sure I’ve noticed that.
Have there been times recently when you felt unusually high, energized, or full of confidence?
Not really… I mean, I’ve had days where I’m keyed up or on edge, but not like… unusually confident or high, no.
Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of your mind?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in or taken out. It’s more… like they’re watching what I do through the route system, and then people make comments on the radio that line up too much. Some drivers seem to be reporting on me.
Have you been feeling deeply depressed most of the day?
Not really… I mean, I get down sometimes, but I wouldn’t say deeply depressed most of the day.
Has anyone told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
I don’t think so. People sometimes tell me to slow down or repeat myself, but… I haven’t really been told I’m jumping all over the place.
About how long have you been feeling that people at work are watching you or reporting on you?
I guess… about two months. That’s when it started feeling pretty clear, with the computer system and the radio comments.
Outside of the radio at work, have you heard a voice speaking to you when no one was there?
No… I don’t think so. Not like a voice talking to me when nobody’s there.
Since this started, have you found yourself feeling much less interested in being around other people?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t really feel like doing choir anymore, or having the softball team over like I used to. After work I mostly just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, but I don’t end up starting dinner or calling anyone or… much of anything.
Have you noticed that your emotions feel flatter than usual, like your face or voice shows less feeling than it used to?

Maybe. I don’t really think about my face or voice much. I just… don’t feel like doing things I used to, like choir or having the softball team over. Most days after work I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open and don’t really start anything.
Since these problems began, have they been present for more than one month?
Yeah… more than a month. It’s been kind of building for maybe eight months, since they put me in that temporary dispatch lead spot.
Have you heard two or more voices talking to each other about you?
No… I don’t think so. Not like two voices talking to each other about me.
From when these problems first began, has it been at least six months?
Yeah… it’s been about eight months, I think. Since that temporary dispatch lead thing started.
Since this started, have you been having a hard time getting yourself to start everyday things, even when you mean to?

Yeah… I guess so. After work I’ll sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, like I’m going to make dinner or return calls, and then I just… don’t. I don’t really have people over anymore either, or feel like doing choir or softball stuff.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes persistent persecutory delusions centered on being watched and reported on at work, lasting about 8 months with active symptoms for more than 1 month. There is associated negative symptomatology/functional decline including social withdrawal, loss of interest in prior activities, and reduced initiation of everyday tasks. Mood episodes are denied, and there is no evidence that depression or mania better explains the psychosis. Although hallucinations, thought insertion/withdrawal, and disorganized speech are denied, schizophrenia paranoid type is supported by chronic persecutory psychosis with deterioration in functioning.
